stem:
Ira starts Kaprekar's routine with the 4-digit number $3524$, which has at least two different digits. She forms the largest and smallest numbers from those digits, subtracts, and repeats.

Which two claims correctly describe the routine?

options.text: Any single rearrangement of $3524$ is already the finished Kaprekar result.
From $3524$ she computes $5432 - 2345 = 3087$, then continues the same largest-minus-smallest step on $3087$.
When a step reaches $6174$, the next largest-minus-smallest step stays at $6174$.
The routine also settles every 3-digit starter by the same $6174$ stop.

teacher.key_rationale: Kaprekar's 4-digit step is largest minus smallest from the same digits, repeated until 6174, which then repeats. One rearrangement alone is not the routine; extending the 6174 stop to every 3-digit starter overreaches the rule.
